question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} x+1 & 2 \\ 0 & x-3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} x & 2 \\ 0 & x \end{bmatrix}$, find $A^2 - 2AB + B^2$.
explanation:
First compute $A^2$, $AB$ and $B^2$.

$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} (x+1)^2 & 4x-4 \\ 0 & (x-3)^2 \end{bmatrix}$.

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x^2+x & 4x+2 \\ 0 & x^2-3x \end{bmatrix}$.

$2AB = \begin{bmatrix} 2x^2+2x & 8x+4 \\ 0 & 2x^2-6x \end{bmatrix}$.

$B^2 = \begin{bmatrix} x^2 & 4x \\ 0 & x^2 \end{bmatrix}$.

Now $A^2 - 2AB + B^2$ gives:

$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -8 \\ 0 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$.
